body: Wendy: Every Witch Way is WayForward's Game Boy Color platformer starring Wendy the Good Little Witch from the Casper stories. After magical stones disturb a floating castle's gravity, she travels through its halls, gardens, dungeons and towers to put things right. Switching gravity lets Wendy treat the ceiling as another route, changing how an ordinary arrangement of platforms is understood. The player repeatedly reverses the direction of a fall, using the same small space from two perspectives while avoiding the creatures and hazards occupying it.

A gravity change affects the relationship between Wendy and the architecture around her. A platform that was overhead becomes a possible destination, while another reversal may be needed to leave enough room for the next obstacle. The stages ask the player to plan those changes rather than simply toggle whenever the floor ends. Each world also contains a broom-riding shooting section, giving the journey another pace between the platforming challenges. The familiar witch's equipment and powers provide clear explanations for those different forms of movement.

Matt Bozon directed and helped design the game, drawing inspiration from the gravity-changing action of Metal Storm. Released in 2001, it also detects when the cartridge is running in a Game Boy Advance and opens an additional world for that machine. The original Game Boy Color adventure remains built around a particularly readable idea: the same room can become another problem when falling changes direction. Wendy's cartoon identity makes that change feel like a natural magical ability, allowing the environments to develop the challenge without requiring a more complicated set of controls.
